title: Bible Verses for Fear and Courage | Prayed
headline: Bible verses for fear, for the night before
dek: Twelve verses for when you are frightened of something specific, sorted by whether you need to be told you are not alone, told to move, or told whose you are.
desc: Twelve Bible verses for fear from the World English Bible, grouped for the night before something hard: verses that say you are not alone, verses that tell you to move anyway, and verses about whose you are. With a prayer to write for each.
card: Twelve verses for when you are frightened of something specific, with a prayer to write for each.
intro: Fear is more honest than anxiety. It usually knows what it is afraid of. The surgery is at seven. The court date is Monday. The test comes back this week. That specificity makes fear easier to pray about and harder to pray away, because the thing really is coming.

The Bible says do not be afraid more often than it says almost anything else, and it never says it to people who have nothing to fear. It says it to a man about to lead an army across a river, to exiles, to a girl who has just been told she will bear a child. The verses below are quoted word for word from the World English Bible and grouped by the three things a frightened person needs to hear: you are not alone, go anyway, and you are mine.
Each group ends with a prayer you could write down tonight, dated, so that you can find it again after the thing has happened and see what you were given.

paras: Nearly every do not be afraid in scripture is followed by the same reason, and it is never that the danger is smaller than you think. It is presence. These four are the clearest.

verses.note: The verse most people memorize for fear, and for good reason. Five promises, one condition: none.
Said to Joshua as Moses hands over the job. Goes before you is the part to hold onto. You are not walking into the room first.
The valley is not skipped. It is walked through. The comfort is company, not a detour.
The image is a bird covering its young. Not a fortress, something warmer and closer than that.

sections.pray: I am afraid of tomorrow and I do not want to pretend otherwise. You said you go before me. Go, then. Be in the room before I get there, and stay after I leave.

paras: Some fear needs comfort. Some needs a push. These are the verses for the fear that has started to make decisions for you, the kind that keeps you from the phone call, the appointment, the conversation.

verses.note: It is a command, not a suggestion, and it is given to someone who has every reason to be afraid. Courage here is a thing you are told to do, not a thing you wait to feel.
Paul writing from prison to a younger man who was losing his nerve. Fear is named as a spirit, and it is not the one you were given.
The shortest and most honest verse on this page. When, not if. Fear and trust in the same breath.
A rhetorical question, and the psalmist knows the real answer is quite a lot. He asks it anyway.

sections.pray: I have been letting fear choose for me. I am going to make the call today. Give me the courage you commanded, not the courage I feel, and let that be enough.

paras: The deepest answer to fear in scripture is not a promise about the outcome. It is a statement about who you belong to. These four verses say it in four different ways.

verses.note: Called by your name. You are mine. The verse right after this one is about passing through waters and fire. Belonging comes first.
Abba is the word a small child uses. The opposite of fear, here, is not bravery. It is being someone's.
Two questions with the same answer. If the LORD is your light, there is no one left on the list.
The hardest verse in this group, and worth sitting with. It does not say fear is wrong. It says love, when it is finished with you, will not leave room for it.

sections.pray: Before the outcome, before the answer, I am yours. Say my name over me tonight. Let that settle something that the news tomorrow cannot unsettle.

closing_h2: Date the prayer, then come back to it
closing: Fear has a short memory. The thing you dreaded happens or does not, and either way the dread evaporates, taking with it any record that you were carried. The next fear arrives and you face it as though you have never been through one.

Writing the prayer down, with a date, fixes that. Prayed brings each written prayer back to you at three days, a week, a month and a year, so that the prayer from the night before the surgery is put back in front of you once the surgery is behind you. You can mark it answered, or ongoing, or released, and it stays. Nothing you write leaves your phone.
Pick the verse on this page that is closest to your fear tonight. Write the prayer under it. Date it. That is the whole practice.
